fragments.text:
Dear AC/SPC, our paper explores how to combine Muon with sign compression. We investigate signing before, after or on both sides of orthogonalization and add error feedback to the resulting methods. The exploration identifies different successful choices: SignMuon leads our centralized vision study; EF21-MuonUSign and its bidirectional variant EF21-MuonSign are robust to data heterogeneity in our federated test. We support these findings with convergence guarantees, conditions for SignMuon convergence and explicit failure constructions.

On centralized ResNet18/CIFAR-10 (3 seeds), SignMuon reaches 94.60% versus Muon 94.35% and SignSGD 93.37%. In response to the reviews, we completed learning-rate tuning for all 10 methods on federated CNN2/CIFAR-10 with 11 Dirichlet(0.1) clients, 2000 rounds and no local updates. Rates use 5000 held-out validation images and seed 0, with momentum 0.9. Over 5 final seeds, EF21-MuonSign reaches 84.03±0.52% and EF21-MuonUSign 83.84±0.32%, versus Muon 46.02±8.55% and SignMuon 42.96±5.94%. See our response to 7S1b, Q2 for the full table.

Based on the reviews, we extended EF21-MuonUSign and EF21-MuonSign convergence to fixed EMA/Nesterov and deterministic learning-rate schedules, and verified the tracking and convergence proofs in Lean. The constant/cosine theorems bound expected nuclear gradient norms for exact polar updates under the submitted separable-layer assumption. We separately proved the squared-gradient rate with gradient-dependent steps. Our added SignMuon theorem allows interacting layers under joint smoothness and uniform alignment of signed updates with momentum; measuring this condition during network training remains open.

For D4r2, composing the linear objectives with softplus makes them smooth and lower bounded while preserving ascent for all 3 plain sign placements. For Tx34, we constructed new convex quadratic examples for exact-polar EF21-SignMuon. Their gradients have a nonzero projection onto a fixed direction in parameter space. Every compressed update is perpendicular to that direction. The parameters never change along it, leaving that gradient projection unchanged and the full gradient norm at least 1. This yields failure with rates decreasing to zero: any strictly decreasing schedule without momentum, and shifted power decay with fixed EMA/Nesterov. Separately, for any budget T and any constant rate and fixed momentum chosen for T, a convex quadratic with the same smoothness and initial gap keeps the gradient norm at least 1 throughout. Thus tuning those fixed parameters to the run length also fails to provide a uniform vanishing rate. The exact algebraic certificate has been checked.

For Ueq5 and pqje, the submitted CNN2/CIFAR-10 logs reproduce A8: MuonSign 82.94±0.19% versus SignSGD 81.44±0.15%. We corrected Table 2 and its reversed comparison in the revision. We ask that the exploration of sign-based methods, completed theory extensions and new heterogeneous results be weighed together.
fragments.notes:
Optional scientific synthesis checked against E1/E3/E4/N1/G1/T1. No reliance on J1. Actual confidential field limit/readers remain unknown. New transfer evidence: E5, 50 independently recomputed run histories.
Readability revision: claims about Lean refer to original failure results and EF21 core proofs; see F1. The confidential field limit remains unknown.
Revision 4 foregrounds post-submission heterogeneous results and theory extensions. The full table is in 7S1b Q2. Lean verification covers the core EF21 proofs and original failure results, not the separate conditional SignMuon theorem. Field limit remains unknown.
Revision 5: named every vision setup, highlighted the two EF results, scoped the only-success claim to Muon variants above 80% in the reused-rate test, and explained softplus composition. Core EF21 proofs and original ascent results retain their separate Lean scope; the softplus and N4 extensions are not claimed Lean-verified.
Revision 8: contribution-first prose, no inline bold results, and a mechanism explanation for the quadratic construction. Prior evidence and unknown confidential limit retained.
Revision 9: exploration-first synthesis; fixed direction explicitly defined in parameter space; decreasing schedules and budget-dependent constant-parameter tuning are separate consequences. Observed centralized performance is not claimed to prove per-step neural-network descent.
Revision 10: latest author instruction adds Dear Reviewer greetings and reviewer-specific closings; only pqje (5) and Tx34 (4) have gentle reassessment wording. This explicit instruction takes precedence over the concurrent generic primer suggestion to leave closings empty. Contribution wording describes sign placements and adding EF. Robustness is supported for both EF21-MuonUSign and its bidirectional variant EF21-MuonSign in the tested heterogeneous setting.
Revision 10: the printed fixed-radius/constant-cosine theorem assumes exact polar factors. Its tracking budget separates initialization, movement and noise, with compressor constants. The more general Lean BlockTrajectory.Oracle assumes a spectral-radius bound and <h,D_t(h)> >= gain*||h||_* - delta_t, and expected_stationarity_sum adds sum_t eta_t*delta_t (summed over blocks), normalized by mass in expected_stationarity. This condition exposes approximation loss; it does not certify delta_t for the implemented solver. Earlier notes saying numerical accuracy is quantified must be read with this distinction.
